JAK2 full-length models

Five models of O60674, 1,132 residues · Cα cartoon trace via 3Dmol.js · drag to rotate, scroll to zoom

The open→closed transition moves JH1 and nothing else. FERM–SH2–JH2 is a rigid body in all five structures and every per-domain RMSD between them is 0.10–0.66 Å; the whole difference is where the red JH1 domain sits.

Both models of pair 1 fitted on their JH2 domains, so JH1's displacement is shown in its own frame. Closed in colour, open in grey. JH1 moves 81.9 Å between the two.

The two closed models agree to 1.53 Å although one had no template and the other was built from the mapped JAK1 closed model — the strongest evidence here that the closed state is real rather than a template artefact. Conversely pair 2's open model sits 0.33 Å from the AlphaFold DB model it was templated on: it reproduced its own template, so it is a control, not a second opinion. Its pLDDT of 94.8 reflects that agreement, not quality.

6. AlphaFold DB PAE

Our OpenFold runs use model_1, which emits no PAE. The AlphaFold DB download includes it, and it is the most important caveat on this page. PAE at (i, j) is the error AlphaFold expects in residue j's position when the prediction is aligned on residue i — so the off-diagonal blocks measure confidence in the relative placement of two domains, which per-residue pLDDT cannot express.

Within domains AlphaFold is confident (2.4–5.4 Å). Between FERM and JH1 it is at 21.0 Å, 68% of the 31 Å ceiling — it has essentially no idea where JH1 sits. That does not invalidate a dual-state ΔΔG, since ΔΔG is local and the domains themselves are confidently modelled, but the interface residues that generate the difference between states are in the least certain part of the model.
